name: ABNT NBR 5410 (low-voltage installations)
references: ABNT NBR 5410:2004 (corrected version 2008), Instalações elétricas de baixa tensão
note: Brazil's low-voltage installations: the circuits that need a 30 mA residual-current device (item 5.1.3.2.2), the volumes round a bathtub or a shower and what may stand in each (9.1), a dwelling's least lighting and outlets (9.5.2), the sizing of a circuit's conductors and breaker (Tabelas 36 to 48 and 58, and the voltage drop), the fill of a conduit, and surge protection (5.4.2 and 6.3.5). The numbers are the standard's, the words are ours. A utility's own standard (its service categories, a unit's or a building's demand) is an amendment over this code.

rcd.source: ABNT NBR 5410:2004 (corrected version 2008), item 5.1.3.2.2, additional protection by a residual-current device. Equivalents: IEC 60364-4-41 (411.3.3) and BS 7671 (411.3.3) ask it for outlets up to 32 A whatever the room, and IEC 60364-7-701 and BS 7671 section 701 for every circuit of a room with a bath or a shower; the US NEC (210.8) asks a GFCI, a device of its own, by a list of places much like this one.
rcd.max_outlet_source: NBR 5410:2004, 5.1.3.2.2, note 1: an outlet is reached up to a rated current of 32 A
rcd.it_source: NBR 5410:2004, 5.1.3.2.2, note 2: a circuit or sector of an IT scheme that must not be cut, for the safety of persons or to keep lives, is left out

bath_volumes.source: ABNT NBR 5410:2004 (corrected version 2008), item 9.1, places with a bathtub or a shower (Figures 16 to 18). Equivalents: IEC 60364-7-701 and BS 7671 section 701 answer the same question, but their present editions draw zones 0 to 2 only, with other reaches, so they would be a set of their own rows; the US NEC (410.10(D), 406.9(C)) keeps luminaires and receptacles out of a space over the tub or shower instead.

volumes.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.2.1 a) (the inside of the tub, tray or recess), 9.1.3.1.1 (SELV up to 12 V only, its source outside) and 9.1.4.1 (IPX7)

volumes.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.2.1 b) (over volume 0 to the vertical face around the tub or tray, or 0.6 m around a shower with no tray, up to 2.25 m) and 9.1.4.1 (IPX4)

volumes.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.2.1 c) (0.60 m out from volume 1, from the floor up to 3 m, so over volume 1 too) and 9.1.4.1 (IPX3, IPX5 in a public bathroom)

allows.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.4.3.1 and its note (controls at SELV)

volumes.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.2.1 d) (2.40 m out from volume 2, from the floor up to 2.25 m) and 9.1.4.1 (IPX1, IPX5 in a public bathroom)

allows.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.1.4.3 and 9.1.4.4 (no further limit in volume 3)

bath_volumes.not_covered: fixed walls and partitions, which the volumes go around (note 1 of 9.1.2.1: here the reach is measured straight, so what stands behind one is taken as inside, on the safe side); the space under a tub or tray (note 2); the 0.60 m around the door of a prefabricated shower cabin (9.1.4.3.3); the wiring (9.1.4.2.1 to 9.1.4.2.3); the supplementary equipotential bonding (9.1.3.1.2); and the circuits' own residual-current device, which dr_check asks
